record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: Assume all jobs follow the same speedup function, but their inherent sizes are known when they are scheduled. What allocation policy minimizes mean response time in this known-size parallel scheduling setting?

evidence.quote: In this section, we continue to assume that all jobs follow the same speedup function, but now we assume that the inherent job sizes are all known. Optimizing mean response time in this setting is still a largely open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a parallel scheduling system with $k$ identical servers (cores) and a stream of jobs arriving over time. Each job $j$ has an inherent size $x_j > 0$, which is fully known to the scheduler at the moment of its arrival. All jobs share a common speedup function $s : [0,k] \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, which is nondecreasing, concave, satisfies $s(0)=0$, and specifies the instantaneous service rate of a job when $a \in [0,k]$ servers are allocated to it. At each time $t$, a scheduler must choose a (possibly time-varying) allocation $(a_j(t))_j$ of the $k$ servers among the jobs currently in the system, where $a_j(t) \ge 0$ and $\sum_j a_j(t) \le k$. A job $j$ that arrives at time $r_j$ departs at the first time $c_j$ such that $\int_{r_j}^{c_j} s(a_j(t))\, \mathrm{d}t = x_j$, and its response time is $T_j = c_j - r_j$.

Determine the allocation policy (possibly preemptive, with full knowledge of remaining sizes and elapsed system state) that minimizes the long-run mean response time $\mathbb{E}[T]$ for jobs arriving according to a Poisson process with arbitrary size distribution, under a common concave speedup function $s$. Specifically, characterize the optimal policy and prove its optimality.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem (Poisson arrivals, arbitrary size distribution, general concave speedup) appears largely open. Partial results are known: heSRPT (Berg, Dorsman, Harchol-Balter) gives an optimal allocation minimizing mean slowdown/response time in the all-jobs-present-at-time-0 setting under a common speedup curve, and EQUI is optimal under common speedup with exponential sizes. Recent work (2025) characterizes optimal policies under general concave speedup via a Consistent Derivative Ratio rule, but optimal scheduling for general size distributions with arrivals remains incompletely resolved.

status_evidence.title: heSRPT: Optimal Parallel Scheduling of Jobs With Known Sizes
status_evidence.snippet: heSRPT provides the first optimal allocation policy for minimizing the mean slowdown of parallelizable jobs of known size when all jobs are present at time 0.
status_evidence.claim: Optimality is established only for the special case where all jobs are present at time 0.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Parallel Scheduling under Concave Speedup Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Develops optimal scheduling algorithms for parallel jobs with general concave speedup functions; optimal solution characterized by the Consistent Derivative Ratio (CDR) Rule.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress provides optimality characterizations under concave speedup, but full resolution for the arrival/queueing setting is recent and limited.

status_evidence.title: Towards Optimality in Parallel Job Scheduling
status_evidence.snippet: EQUI is optimal when all jobs follow a single speedup curve and have exponentially distributed sizes.
status_evidence.claim: Known partial result: EQUI optimal in the exponential-size case.
